checks.name: C10 literal direction and smallest intended repair
checks.argument: Under Section 11's partial number-theoretic range-generator convention, from a valid tester index e define a partial program P_e(x): run tester e on x; if its answer is1 output x; otherwise diverge. For every language L with tester e, range(P_e)=L, including L=empty. Inserting e into this fixed program template is a uniform recursive index transformation (ordinary machine parameterization); a constant-in-time approximation is limiting recursive. It works for all valid testers and hence on every source class C, contradicting the literal no tester-to-generator conclusion. The smallest intended direction repair is no limiting-recursive GENERATOR-to-TESTER translation for C. To check the source argument, choose the given infinite recursive L0 in C and restrict to D=all finite languages union {L0}. D is superfinite and consists of recursive/r.e. languages. An assumed generator-to-tester limiting translation on C restricts to D. Source I.7 gives an effective generator learner on primitive-recursive texts for D; the source naming-translation theorem would produce an effective tester learner on those same texts, contrary to source I.9. This last lower-bound check is conditional on those published theorems, whose effective proofs are not formalized/re-audited here.
checks.validation: Informal local program-template/refutation and conditional source-theorem implication; not Lean-checked. Accepted as an intended Section 11 direction correction, not a certificate for the whole corrected lower bound.
checks.boundary: If generator is instead required to be a TOTAL enumeration with no blank, empty L has no generator. source_correspondence.source_claim: ANY superfinite class is NOT EFFECTIVELY tester-identifiable from primitive recursive text. The source allows any infinite witness L and says if it is nonrecursive it has no tester, otherwise use a primitive recursive range enumeration f of L. The diagonal construction is scoped: after replacing a computable guessing functional by a primitive recursive approximation with the same limiting behavior (cited Gold1965), maintain X_t and output i_t; P_t means f(X_t) has already appeared, Q_t means a bounded computation witness y<=t shows current tester guess rejects f(X_t). Start X_1=1 and i_1=f(1). Advance X when P; produce f(X) when not P and Q; otherwise repeat the preceding output. Both the primitive recursiveness of this generated text and its eventual failure of stable correct testing matter. Cases can yield a finite target or the infinite L; no semantic impossibility is claimed. Proof text pp.472-473 case II visually reads an x OUTSIDE the finite produced range with Z_a(x)!=0; OCR corrupts its membership signs. This is not a reason to change the theorem statement.
